about: What calls on the runtime conformance plugin (conformance-weather) return: one list that both the real runtimes and the SDK testing tools are checked against (issue #206, risk A1, Q6.7.2).

Real runtimes: rutis_bridge::runtime::testing::runtime (crates/rutis-bridge/tests/session_matrix.rs). Testing tools: node/rutis/test/conformance.test.mjs (@arcships/rutis/testing) and python/rutis/tests/test_conformance.py (rutis.testing), in strict mode, and go/rutis/rutistest/conformance_test.go (rutistest).
The plugin injects `clock`, whose `now()` returns 0, 1, 2, ... one per call, and provides `service` with `methods`.

A call: `call` (method), `args` (JSON; {"$callback": ...} is a function the caller passes: "upper" returns its argument upper-cased; {"throws": {name, message, fields}} throws an error with that name and message and extra `fields`), and what it does: `returns` (a JSON value; keys in `ignore` are not compared; `copied`: it is not the object passed in), `throws` ({} for any error, or the `name` and `message` the caller receives; the thrown error's extra `fields` do not cross) or `exits` (the plugin's process exits with this status).
`samples` are values one language makes: the plugin's `samples()` names the ones it has, `sample(name)` returns one; a runtime whose plugin has no `samples` method has none.

`events` (after `calls` and `samples`): the host emits `emit` with `args` (JSON) as Process::emit does, the runtime mounted with `emits`; then `then` is a call as in `calls`, or the emission `throws`. The session matrix requires these checks on Node, Bun, Python and Go; the Node and Python testing tools also check them.
`allowed`: the testing tool does not do what this entry says, and why (a bounded, written-down difference, also in docs/guide/plugin-api.md). Every other entry holds for both.

Tagged values (#308, docs/design-value-types-2026-10-15.md) are written {"$<tag>": <the value's wire text>}: {"$instant": "2026-10-15T03:22:15.123Z"}, {"$bytes": "aGVsbG8="} (base64), {"$map": [[key, value], ...]}, {"$set": [element, ...]}, and so for datetime, date, time, bigint, decimal and uuid. No plain value is written so.

`pending`: no runtime's plugin names this sample yet; a runtime names it in its `samples()` once it sends that value (#308 phase 3), and the entry then holds for it like any other. Until then it is not checked.

calls.why: a sync call that calls a host service
the host service is called on every call
a callback during a sync call
an error crosses twice (callback to plugin, plugin to caller) with its name and message, not as the object thrown
data crosses both ways as a copy

calls.allowed: the testing tool runs the plugin in the test's own process, so a plugin that ends its process ends the test: the tool cannot show this, and tests do not call it

events.why: a leaf listener receives a declared host event, and its effect is visible to the next call

throws.message: event weather/undeclared is not declared for emission from rutis

events.why: only events declared in emits can be sent

samples.why: a Date does not cross
a Map does not cross
binary data (a Uint8Array) does not cross
a number that is not finite does not cross
undefined inside data arrives as null
an Error returned as a value arrives as data: its name, message and stack
a tuple arrives as a list
a dataclass arrives as a dict
a set does not cross
bytes do not cross
a float that is not finite does not cross
a dict with keys that are not strings does not cross
an exception returned as a value arrives as data: its name and message
integers within ±(2^53−1) cross, and a bool stays a bool
an integer beyond ±(2^53−1) does not cross (#356): past 2^64 Rust would read it as a float, past 2^53 JavaScript cannot hold it exactly
nor does one inside data
a Date (new Date('2026-10-15T03:22:15.123Z')) arrives as an instant
a Uint8Array arrives as bytes
a Map arrives as a map, its keys of different kinds kept apart and in order, undefined as null
a Set arrives as a set, in order
a bigint arrives as a big integer
the SDK constructors send a datetime, date, time, decimal and uuid; the decimal keeps its trailing zero
a Map keyed by a Date does not cross: a Date compares by identity as a key (design §5)
a datetime with a time zone arrives as an instant in UTC, to the microsecond
a datetime without a time zone arrives as a local datetime, not read in any zone (design V5)
a Decimal and a UUID arrive as values, not as object references (#355)
a dict with integer keys arrives as a map
a time.Time arrives as an instant in UTC, to the nanosecond
a []byte inside a struct arrives as bytes, not as base64 text (V9)
a time.Time inside a struct (here at +02:00) arrives as an instant in UTC, not as RFC 3339 text in its zone (V9)
a map with integer keys arrives as a map, its keys in order
a map[K]struct{} arrives as a set, its elements in order
a *big.Int arrives as a big integer
rutis.DateTime, Date, TimeOfDay, Decimal and UUID arrive as a datetime, date, time, decimal and uuid; the decimal keeps its trailing zero
an integer beyond ±(2^53−1) inside a struct does not cross (V9): encoding/json did not check it
